lessonTitle: Pick your training route
title: Create your evidence folder
where: Physical Windows host / File Explorer / lab notes; no Azure deployment.
actions: On the physical host, open File Explorer and create a SONIC-Lab folder with subfolders Installers, Screenshots, Baselines, and Backups. Keep passwords elsewhere.
expected: The four folders exist on storage with sufficient free space.

lessonTitle: Pick your training route
title: Record the version journey
where: Physical Windows host / File Explorer / lab notes; no Azure deployment.
actions: Create a lab note: VMware Workstation Pro on the host; Windows Server 2019 Desktop Experience on premises; Server 2019 Azure destination; migrate test workload/data; then upgrade that Azure member server to Server 2022.
expected: Your note distinguishes moving an application from moving a whole VM.

lessonTitle: Pick your training route
title: Choose the required route
where: Physical Windows host / File Explorer / lab notes; no Azure deployment.
actions: Complete the Windows/AD core, SQL core, Azure foundations, and migration core in sidebar order. Leave MECM and high availability extensions until their prerequisites pass.
expected: DC01/DC02 and APP01 are prepared before the migration work.

lessonTitle: Understand the map
title: Record the named outcome
where: Physical Windows host / lab worksheet; read-only planning.
actions: # Understand the map
expected: Compare your recorded result with the named lesson evidence before marking verified.

lessonTitle: Prepare your laptop and downloads
title: Confirm Workstation Pro
where: Physical Windows host / Workstation Pro / official ISO download; authorized local administrator for installation.
actions: On your physical Windows PC, open VMware Workstation Pro > Help > About. Record the installed version. This course uses Workstation, not vCenter or ESXi.
expected: The product is Workstation Pro and it can create Windows Server 2019 guests.

lessonTitle: Prepare your laptop and downloads
title: Obtain Server 2019 media
where: Physical Windows host / Workstation Pro / official ISO download; authorized local administrator for installation.
actions: Use the Windows Server 2019 ISO your course or license administrator supplies. For local-only evaluation, open https://www.microsoft.com/evalcenter/evaluate-windows-server-2019 and download the 64-bit ISO. Save it under Installers.
expected: The media is Windows Server 2019, not 2025.

lessonTitle: Prepare your laptop and downloads
title: Choose the media and license path
where: Physical Windows host / Workstation Pro / official ISO download; authorized local administrator for installation.
actions: Record language, edition, evaluation/licensed status, and whether Desktop Experience is available. The Azure upgrade exercise uses a licensed/pay-as-you-go 2019 Marketplace member VM with a matching 2022 upgrade path.
expected: Your source and destination license choices are written down.

lessonTitle: Prepare your laptop and downloads
title: Check host resources
where: Physical Windows host / Workstation Pro / official ISO download; authorized local administrator for installation.
actions: On the host press Ctrl+Shift+Esc > Performance. Record available RAM and disk space. Plan roughly 4 GB RAM per DC and APP01, with more for SQL; run optional servers only when the host can accommodate them.
expected: The host has enough free resources for the next required pair of VMs.

lessonTitle: Build one safe VMware network
title: Open the network editor
where: Physical Windows host / Workstation Pro Virtual Network Editor; authorized host administrator.
actions: On the physical host open Workstation Pro > Edit > Virtual Network Editor. Click Change Settings if shown and approve the local Windows administrator prompt.
expected: You can edit virtual-network settings.

lessonTitle: Build one safe VMware network
title: Create a dedicated NAT VMnet
where: Physical Windows host / Workstation Pro Virtual Network Editor; authorized host administrator.
actions: Click Add Network. Choose an unused VMnet, for example VMnet2. Select NAT. Do not edit the VMnet used by unrelated VMs.
expected: A dedicated NAT network appears in the list.

lessonTitle: Build one safe VMware network
title: Set a non-overlapping subnet
where: Physical Windows host / Workstation Pro Virtual Network Editor; authorized host administrator.
actions: For the example plan set Subnet IP to 192.168.77.0 and Subnet mask to 255.255.255.0 only after checking it does not overlap your host, home router, VPN, or Azure address range.
expected: Your chosen lab subnet is private and does not overlap another route you use.

lessonTitle: Build one safe VMware network
title: Record the actual NAT gateway
where: Physical Windows host / Workstation Pro Virtual Network Editor; authorized host administrator.
actions: Click NAT Settings. Read the Gateway IP and write it down exactly, then close the dialog. Do not assume it ends in .1 or .2.
expected: Your worksheet has VMnet name, subnet, mask, and gateway.

lessonTitle: Build one safe VMware network
title: Reserve the static lab addresses
where: Physical Windows host / Workstation Pro Virtual Network Editor; authorized host administrator.
actions: Open DHCP Settings and reserve a static range outside its lease pool, or disable VMware DHCP for this dedicated static-only lab. Plan .10 AG-DC01, .11 AG-DC02, .20 APP01, .60 SQL01, and .70 MECM01 within the chosen /24. Apply and close.
expected: No static server address overlaps a DHCP lease or another server.

lessonTitle: Build one safe VMware network
title: Attach each guest to this VMnet
where: Physical Windows host / Workstation Pro Virtual Network Editor; authorized host administrator.
actions: With a lab VM powered off, right-click it > Settings > Network Adapter. Choose Custom and your recorded VMnet. Enable Connect at power on.
expected: All on-prem lab servers use the same dedicated VMnet.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Open the new VM wizard
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: On your physical Windows PC, open VMware Workstation Pro. Click File, then New Virtual Machine. Do not do this inside another VM.
expected: The New Virtual Machine Wizard is open.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Choose Typical
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Select Typical (recommended), then Next. The reference image has Custom selected; use the upper Typical radio button for this lab.
expected: The wizard asks how the guest operating system will be installed.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Use manual Windows installation
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Select I will install the operating system later, then Next. This avoids Easy Install silently choosing an edition.
expected: The wizard lets you choose a guest OS profile.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Choose the Server 2019 guest profile
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Select Microsoft Windows. Open Version and choose Windows Server 2019, then Next.
expected: The guest profile says Windows Server 2019.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Name the VM
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Enter AG-DC01 as the virtual machine name. Browse to a folder with enough free space, such as your dedicated SONIC lab folder, then Next.
expected: The summary uses AG-DC01 and a location you can find again.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Create a new virtual disk
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Set Maximum disk size to 60 GB for this lab plan. Choose Split virtual disk into multiple files, then Next. Do not attach an existing production disk.
expected: A new blank virtual disk is selected.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Set memory and CPU
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Click Customize Hardware. Select Memory and enter 4096 MB. Select Processors and use 1 processor with 2 cores for the basic lab.
expected: The hardware list shows your memory allocation and two virtual cores.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Attach the Server 2019 ISO
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Select CD/DVD in the hardware list. Choose Use ISO image file, Browse to your Windows Server 2019 ISO, and enable Connect at power on.
expected: The CD/DVD path ends with your Server 2019 ISO filename.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Attach the private VMnet
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Select Network Adapter. Choose Custom: Specific virtual network and the NAT VMnet recorded in LAB 03. Enable Connected and Connect at power on.
expected: The VM is attached to the same private lab VMnet as the other lab servers.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Finish and start the VM
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Click Close, then Finish. Select the new VM in the Workstation library and click Power on this virtual machine. Click inside its console and press a key when the ISO boot prompt appears.
expected: Windows Setup appears inside the VM console.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Start Windows Setup
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Choose the language you need for the course, time format, and keyboard, then Next and Install now. Use English (United States) media if you will follow the Azure upgrade-media route later.
expected: Setup displays an edition list or asks for a legitimate product key.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Choose Desktop Experience
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Select Windows Server 2019 Standard (Desktop Experience), or the matching authorized Datacenter (Desktop Experience) edition your course supplies. If using Evaluation for local practice, record that limitation. Click Next and accept the license only if you agree.
expected: The selected line explicitly includes 2019 and Desktop Experience.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Install only on the new blank disk
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Choose Custom: Install Windows only (advanced). Select the new VM’s blank Drive 0 unallocated space and click Next. This is a clean install in a new VM, not the later Azure in-place upgrade.
expected: Windows copies files, installs, and restarts.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Create the local Administrator password
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: At Customize settings, set and confirm a strong local Administrator password. Save it in your own password manager, then Finish.
expected: The Windows sign-in screen appears.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Sign into the guest
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Use Workstation VM > Send Ctrl+Alt+Del (or Ctrl+Alt+Insert), then sign in as the guest’s local Administrator.
expected: You see a Windows desktop and Server Manager.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Install VMware Tools
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: In Workstation select VM > Install VMware Tools. In the guest open File Explorer > This PC, open the VMware Tools CD, and run setup64.exe if offered. Choose the normal setup and restart when asked.
expected: After restart, the guest is usable with the expected mouse/display integration.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Patch the new Server 2019 guest
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Inside the guest open Start > Settings > Update & Security > Windows Update. Check for updates and restart as required before changing its DNS to the new lab domain.
expected: Windows has completed its pending restarts.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Rename Windows
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Inside the guest press Win+R, enter sysdm.cpl, and press Enter. On Computer Name choose Change. Enter AG-DC01, confirm OK, and restart when prompted.
expected: After signing in again, hostname returns AG-DC01.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Open the guest IPv4 settings
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Inside the guest press Win+R, type ncpa.cpl, and press Enter. Right-click the connected Ethernet adapter > Properties. Select Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4), then Properties.
expected: The IPv4 address and DNS fields are visible.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Enter the lab address
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: For the example LAB 03 network only, choose Use the following IP address: 192.168.77.10; subnet mask 255.255.255.0; gateway = the NAT gateway you recorded in LAB 03. Set preferred DNS to 192.168.77.10. Click OK and Close. If you changed the subnet in LAB 03, use your matching address plan instead.
expected: ipconfig /all shows the chosen private address, gateway, and DNS on the connected adapter.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Confirm this is Server 2019
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Open Start, search Windows PowerShell, right-click it > Run as administrator. Run the read-only inventory below in this VM.
expected: WindowsProductName identifies Windows Server 2019; hostname identifies AG-DC01.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Open Add Roles and Features
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Inside the named server open Server Manager. Choose Manage > Add Roles and Features. Click Next on Before you begin.
expected: The Select installation type page is shown.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Select the local destination server
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Choose Role-based or feature-based installation > Next. Select a server from the server pool and select this VM’s computer name > Next.
expected: The Server Roles page targets the correct computer.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Select AD DS and its tools
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Check Active Directory Domain Services. In the pop-up click Add Features, then Next.
expected: AD DS is selected and its required management tools are included.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Install the role
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Keep the required Features selected. Click Next through the AD DS information page, review the selected target, then click Install.
expected: Installation succeeds and offers Promote this server to a domain controller.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Choose the correct promotion operation
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Click Promote this server to a domain controller. Choose Add a new forest. Enter agency.test as Root domain name. Click Next.
expected: The wizard shows a NEW forest named agency.test.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Set controller options and DSRM
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: For Server 2019 in this lab, use Windows Server 2016 for both forest and domain functional levels. Keep DNS server and Global Catalog selected. Set and confirm a unique DSRM recovery password, store it securely, then Next.
expected: Required options are selected and the password boxes have no validation error.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Review DNS and additional options
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Continue past the isolated-root DNS-delegation warning only if it is the expected warning for this private lab. Confirm the AGENCY NetBIOS name on Additional Options.
expected: The wizard advances without a blocking validation error.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Keep the default AD paths
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: On Paths keep the default NTDS database/log and SYSVOL locations for this small lab, then Next.
expected: The wizard shows Review Options.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Check prerequisites before promotion
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: On Review Options confirm agency.test, the correct computer, and DNS. Click Next, then wait for Prerequisites Check.
expected: The prerequisite check succeeds; only understood lab warnings remain.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Promote and wait for restart
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Click Install only after the prerequisite check passes. Wait for the VM to restart; do not power it off to shorten the wait.
expected: The guest restarts and offers a domain sign-in.

lessonTitle: Make AG-DC01: the agency begins
title: Verify the directory
where: Physical host Workstation Pro, then AG-DC01 guest / Server 2019 Desktop Experience / local Administrator, then AGENCY domain Administrator.
actions: Sign in with your authorized agency.test administrator account. Open Windows PowerShell as administrator in this VM and run the checks.
expected: The DNSRoot is agency.test and domain-controller records resolve to the lab’s private IPs.

lessonTitle: Create test users, OUs, and a GPO
title: Open Active Directory Users and Computers
where: AG-DC01 guest / Server Manager, ADUC, and GPMC / authorized agency.test administrator.
actions: Inside AG-DC01 open Server Manager > Tools > Active Directory Users and Computers. Expand agency.test in the left pane.
expected: You are managing the agency.test directory on AG-DC01.

lessonTitle: Create test users, OUs, and a GPO
title: Create the Operations OU
where: AG-DC01 guest / Server Manager, ADUC, and GPMC / authorized agency.test administrator.
actions: Right-click agency.test > New > Organizational Unit. Enter Operations. Leave protection from accidental deletion enabled, then OK. Repeat to create Security.
expected: Both OUs appear under agency.test.

lessonTitle: Create test users, OUs, and a GPO
title: Create the test user
where: AG-DC01 guest / Server Manager, ADUC, and GPMC / authorized agency.test administrator.
actions: Right-click Operations > New > User. Enter a fictional name and user logon name test.analyst. Click Next, set a private temporary password, choose your lab password-change requirement, Next, then Finish.
expected: test.analyst appears in Operations.

lessonTitle: Create test users, OUs, and a GPO
title: Create and populate the group
where: AG-DC01 guest / Server Manager, ADUC, and GPMC / authorized agency.test administrator.
actions: Right-click Operations > New > Group. Name it GG-Operations, select Global and Security, then OK. Open the group > Members > Add; enter test.analyst > Check Names > OK.
expected: Members lists the new test user.

lessonTitle: Create test users, OUs, and a GPO
title: Open Group Policy Management
where: AG-DC01 guest / Server Manager, ADUC, and GPMC / authorized agency.test administrator.
actions: In Server Manager choose Tools > Group Policy Management. Expand Forest: agency.test > Domains > agency.test.
expected: The Operations OU appears in the policy tree.

lessonTitle: Create test users, OUs, and a GPO
title: Create and link the GPO
where: AG-DC01 guest / Server Manager, ADUC, and GPMC / authorized agency.test administrator.
actions: Right-click Operations > Create a GPO in this domain, and Link it here. Name it LAB-Operations-Banner and click OK.
expected: The named GPO is linked under Operations.

lessonTitle: Create test users, OUs, and a GPO
title: Edit the logon banner
where: AG-DC01 guest / Server Manager, ADUC, and GPMC / authorized agency.test administrator.
actions: Right-click the linked GPO > Edit. Expand Computer Configuration > Policies > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies > Security Options. Set the interactive logon message title to AGENCY LAB and message text to This is a practice environment.
expected: The two banner settings show your lab text.

lessonTitle: Create test users, OUs, and a GPO
title: Verify the objects
where: AG-DC01 guest / Server Manager, ADUC, and GPMC / authorized agency.test administrator.
actions: On AG-DC01 run these read-only checks and capture ADUC plus the GPO link.
expected: The user, group membership, and GPO are returned.

lessonTitle: Allow SSH from your home connection
title: Start on your own Windows computer
where: Your Windows computer at home · web browser
actions:
Use the Windows computer you will use to connect to the lab. Open your browser and go to https://portal.azure.com. Sign in with the Azure account used in the earlier lessons.
You will create the rule by clicking in the Azure website. PowerShell will only help you write down one value. You do not need Azure Cloud Shell, an administrator PowerShell window, or a connection to RHEL for this lesson.
An NSG, short for Network Security Group, is a list of network traffic rules. Inbound means coming into the Azure VM. Outbound means leaving it. Your connection leaves your Windows computer and arrives at the VM, so the VM needs an INBOUND rule.
SSH is the secure connection you will use to type commands on Linux from Windows. Port 22 is the numbered connection point SSH normally uses. This rule lets your home connection reach that point. You still need the correct username and SSH key to sign in.
expected: The Azure website is open on your own Windows computer. You know why this is an inbound rule.

Click the search box at the top of the Azure page. Type Network security groups. Click Network security groups in the results. Click Create.
For Subscription, select the subscription recorded earlier. For Resource group, select rg-rhel9-lab. For Name, type nsg-rhel9-lab. For Region, choose the same region as your lab network.
Click Review + create. Read the names once more. Click Create. Wait for the completion message, then click Go to resource. If that button is missing, search Network security groups again and click nsg-rhel9-lab.
If nsg-rhel9-lab already exists from your earlier work, open it and inspect it instead of creating another one.

lessonTitle: Allow SSH from your home connection
title: Find the public address of your home connection
where: Your Windows computer · Azure website · nsg-rhel9-lab

where: Your own Windows computer · Windows Terminal → PowerShell · normal user
actions:

Connection timed out means start with the VM power state, correct IP, inbound TCP 22 rule and network route. Connection refused usually means the destination was reached but no service accepted the port, or a device actively rejected it. Changing key permissions will not fix those problems.

title: Inspect the owner and who can read the key
where: Your own Windows computer · Windows Terminal → PowerShell · normal user
actions:
icacls lists the file’s permission entries. R means read, W means write, M means modify, F means full control, and I means inherited from the parent folder. Inheritance means a file receives permissions from its folder.
Get-Acl shows the owner and a table of entries. Allow gives access; Deny blocks access. Check the file itself and its parent folder. Removing inheritance does not remove permissions that were added directly to the file.
For your personal client key, use your own account as owner and restrict access to that account under workplace policy. Reading is enough for SSH to use it. Other ordinary users or shared groups should not read it. Do not copy Windows SSH server authorized_keys permission recipes onto this personal private key.
If the owner is another account, the file is centrally managed, or access is denied, stop and ask the Windows administrator to repair this exact file. Do not take ownership of a folder tree. If elevation is required, reopen PowerShell with Run as administrator under the intended identity and recheck whoami first.
Keep keys under %USERPROFILE%\.ssh, outside OneDrive and the repository. If this key is in a synced/shared folder, arrange a move to that local folder while preserving working access. After moving it, repeat the path-selection and inspection cards with its new path before continuing. Moving it does not erase older shared or cloud copies; replace an exposed key through your normal key-rotation process.
expected: You know the owner, your account SID and the exact unwanted entries before changing anything.

where: Your own Windows computer · Windows Terminal → PowerShell · normal user
actions:

Push-Location temporarily opens the key’s parent folder so the saved filename can be restored to the same folder later. Pop-Location returns to your previous folder.
If saving fails, stop. Do not continue with an unknown recovery path.
expected: The permission backup was saved successfully and its path is recorded.

title: Give your own account read access, then remove inherited entries
where: Your own Windows computer · Windows Terminal → PowerShell · normal user
actions:
Use this only for the personally owned key checked above. Run one line at a time. /grant:r replaces the explicit Allow entry for this SID only. It does not remove other users, groups or Deny entries.
The * tells icacls that the value is a numeric SID. R gives read access. Adding your explicit entry first avoids removing your only inherited access.
/inheritance:r turns off inheritance and removes inherited entries from this file. It does not touch every file in the folder. Stop on any error.
expected: Your explicit read entry exists. Review any remaining explicit entries in the next step.

lessonTitle: Create and inspect the rexuser key pair
title: Remove only a confirmed unwanted explicit entry
where: Your own Windows computer · Windows Terminal → PowerShell · normal user
actions:
If the permission list still shows an unwanted account or group, copy its exact SID from the error or identify it with the Windows administrator. Do not enter your own SID. Do not remove entries from a whole folder tree.
S-1-5-32 identifies the Windows BUILTIN domain; it is not a universal name for every built-in group. Use the exact offending entry shown for your file. Do not copy another person’s account SID from a screenshot.
The command below removes entries for the chosen SID only. Run it once per reviewed unwanted entry, then inspect the list again. If the remaining entries are unclear or policy-managed, use the administrator rather than guessing.
GUI alternative: File Explorer → the exact key → right-click → Properties → Security → Advanced. Check Owner. Select only an unwanted permission entry → Remove. Keep your account’s Read entry → Apply → OK. Inspect again. Do not reset the whole folder.
Do not use /reset as the normal fix: it replaces the file’s permissions with inherited defaults and can make the key readable by others again.
expected: Only the intended personal-key access remains. No shared group or unrelated user can read the key.

title: Command 1: read, type, then check

actions:
# makes each example a shell comment. These placeholders demonstrate methods; they are not a request to install anything now.
chmod changes permission bits. u+x adds execute permission for the owner only. ./script.sh uses ./ to mean a file in the current directory, not one found through PATH. Review contents, source, integrity, and required interpreter before execution.
bash ./script.sh is an alternative that asks Bash to read the script; it normally needs read permission rather than an execute bit. It does not make a malicious script safe, and not every .sh file is meant for Bash.
sudo requests privileged execution. dnf install ./package.rpm installs a local RPM and resolves dependencies through configured repositories; ./ distinguishes the local file from a repository package name. Review package signature/source and the transaction before confirming.
tar handles archives. -t lists members, -x extracts, -z processes gzip compression, and -f says the next argument is the archive filename. Use listing before extraction and an empty staging directory; untrusted paths, links, or overwrite targets need review. Extraction alone does not install software.
Repository-based dnf install package-name selects a named package from enabled repositories. Trust the repository and package signatures, inspect the proposed transaction, and record the exact installed version.

lessonTitle: Checkpoint: what is your rollback plan?
title: Before anything changes: decide exactly what to back up
where: Work administration workstation · change record and Veeam console (12 or 13)
actions:
Start with the VM you will change: select its whole-VM backup, including the OS disk and every data disk used by the application. For a new RHEL installation, back up the clean, working VM before installing Wazuh. After successful installation and verification, create a new accepted baseline; retain the pre-change recovery point according to policy.
If the change affects AD, DNS, domain membership or Group Policy, verify a recent application-aware backup of the domain controller first, including the volumes containing AD DS, SYSVOL and DNS-related state. Record domain-recovery access and the approved AD recovery procedure. A DNS export or GPO export alone cannot recover a domain controller. Do not casually revert a production domain controller snapshot.
For the Wazuh central host, include its OS, configuration, certificates, enrollment material and all disks containing indexer/event data. If manager, indexer and dashboard are separate VMs, identify all of them. A live disk copy is not automatically a consistent Wazuh/indexer backup: use the application recovery procedure or a coordinated clean shutdown in an approved outage. Do not independently restore mismatched cluster members.
For the RHEL endpoint or Windows client, include the OS, application data and agent configuration before agent installation, realm changes or hardening. Record its current manager association so recovery does not leave duplicate or stale enrollment. Back up only the affected systems and dependencies; an endpoint-only change does not require backing up every enterprise VM.
Save a protected change record outside the changed VM: hostnames, IP/DNS settings, disk inventory, package/kernel versions, service status, relevant configuration and rollback triggers. Keep credentials, private keys and recovery passwords in approved secret storage, never in the course GitHub repository. File hashes and screenshots are evidence, not backups.
expected: A named list of affected VMs, all required disks, dependencies and application-consistency requirements exists before a backup job is selected.

lessonTitle: Checkpoint: what is your rollback plan?
title: Verify the backup scope and recovery access before taking a snapshot
where: Veeam Backup & Replication 12/13 · console
actions:
Open Home → Jobs → Backup. Select the existing job → Edit. On Virtual Machines, confirm the exact VM is included; inspect exclusions and disk selection so required data disks are not omitted. Inspect Storage for the intended repository and retention. Use Cancel after read-only inspection; have the backup owner apply any required job changes.
For a Windows domain controller, inspect Guest Processing → application-aware processing and the per-VM application settings. Confirm guest credentials and processing success in the completed session, rather than merely seeing a checked option. Windows AD processing does not make an arbitrary Linux application consistent.
Check that the backup repository is outside the VM being changed, has capacity and remains reachable during recovery. Confirm the restore operator can access the backup and its encryption password independently of the affected machine/domain. Follow the workplace policy for an independent protected or immutable copy.
Ask the backup owner to verify the Veeam server configuration backup too. In the main menu select Configuration Backup and inspect its latest success, repository and encryption setting. This protects backup configuration; it does not replace VM backups. Store its encryption password separately in approved storage. Do not change enterprise backup settings as part of an endpoint lesson.
Run the approved VM backup using the later cards, verify the new per-VM restore point, and record a tested restore route. Only then take a short-lived vSphere snapshot immediately before the change if required. Backup first, temporary snapshot second, change third. This is a pre-change protection order, not a universal disaster-recovery restore order.
expected: The current restore point covers the intended data, recovery access works, and application-specific restore limitations are recorded. Unknown coverage is a no-go.

lessonTitle: Checkpoint: what is your rollback plan?

Open Snapshots → Manage Snapshots and inspect existing checkpoints. Check datastore free space and whether a backup job is running. Coordinate the maintenance window with the backup owner; do not take or remove a checkpoint during an active backup.
Record change scope, rollback trigger, maximum diagnosis time, snapshot expiry, backup restore point and validation steps. This RHEL procedure is not a domain-controller recovery procedure: AD needs application-aware/system-state recovery planning and identity consistency.
expected: The change targets one identified RHEL VM and has an independent backup/recovery plan.

lessonTitle: Checkpoint: what is your rollback plan?
title: At work: create a short-lived vSphere snapshot
where: Work administration workstation · vSphere Client
actions:
Right-click the selected VM → Snapshots → Take Snapshot. Enter a unique name containing the change ID and time, and a description of the pre-change state.
For a planned cold checkpoint, shut down the guest cleanly first and confirm Powered off. Memory capture does not apply while powered off. For an approved powered-on checkpoint, decide whether memory capture is needed; it increases size/time. Filesystem quiescing requires working VMware Tools and is not automatically application-consistent backup.
Select Create/OK. Watch Recent Tasks until the snapshot task succeeds, then reopen Manage Snapshots to confirm its name/time. Record the evidence before starting the change.
Keep snapshots brief and remove them after validation and approval. Broadcom advises not retaining a single snapshot beyond 72 hours; workplace policy can require a shorter period. Snapshot deltas depend on base disks, so they are not standalone backups.
expected: The intended checkpoint exists and its owner, expiry and consistency limitations are recorded.

lessonTitle: Checkpoint: what is your rollback plan?
title: At work: choose fix, revert or restore from backup
where: Work administration workstation · change record and vSphere Client
actions:
If the change works, validate the application and document the result. If it fails, preserve logs and make one evidence-based correction within the agreed time. If risk grows or the time expires, stop and execute the recorded recovery branch.
For an approved snapshot revert: right-click the exact VM → Snapshots → Manage Snapshots. Select the recorded pre-change checkpoint → Revert. Read the warning about losing later changes and confirm only within the approved outage/data-loss scope. Verify power state, guest access, storage and application behavior afterward.
For cleanup after a successful change: select the checkpoint → Delete. Deleting merges snapshot changes; it does not restore the earlier state. Monitor the task and datastore capacity. Do not select Delete All merely to remove one checkpoint.
If snapshots cannot meet the recovery requirement, use the enterprise backup restore plan. Test a recovery to an isolated destination when possible; never connect a duplicate restored identity to production by accident.
expected: Recovery is judged by validated guest/application state, not just a completed hypervisor task.

lessonTitle: Checkpoint: what is your rollback plan?

actions:
Open the Veeam console → Help → About and record the product, version and build. These command names refer to Veeam Backup & Replication VMware VM jobs; Veeam Agent jobs and other Veeam products use different cmdlets.
Open the PowerShell session supplied with the installed Veeam console. Run Get-Command to discover what is available, then Get-Help for the local syntax. Do not run these in the RHEL terminal or assume ordinary Windows PowerShell already has the Veeam module.
Get-VBRJob inspects VM jobs; Get-VBRBackupSession inspects execution history; Get-VBRRestorePoint inspects recovery points. Starting a job is a separate authorized operation, not proof of recovery. The exact start/restore walkthrough must match your workplace version and job type.
expected: The product/build and supported local command syntax are identified before any backup job is changed or started.

lessonTitle: Checkpoint: what is your rollback plan?
title: At work: inspect one existing VMware backup job
where: Veeam Backup & Replication · Veeam PowerShell session
actions:
This example targets an existing VMware VM backup job, not a Veeam Agent policy. Verify these cmdlets in your installed version first. In the console select Home → Jobs → Backup and copy the exact approved job name.
Enter that name at the prompt. Get-VBRJob retrieves jobs; Where-Object keeps only an exact name match. The count check stops an ambiguous selection. Review the returned job in the console and confirm it includes the intended VM, the correct repository, retention and application-processing settings.
Get-VBRBackupSession lists history. It does not create a backup. Inspect the job session and per-VM task results in History; an old successful run is not proof of a current restore point.
expected: One reviewed job is selected and its VM membership and recent task results are understood.

lessonTitle: Checkpoint: what is your rollback plan?

where: Veeam Backup & Replication · same PowerShell session and console

In the console open History → Jobs and select the new session. Wait for completion and inspect the intended VM task result. Investigate Warning or Failed; do not count a job merely starting as success.
Open Home → Backups → Disk, expand the backup and locate the intended VM. Inspect its restore points and record the new timestamp, repository and retention. Arrange an isolated restore rehearsal under the workplace restore procedure; a successful backup job alone does not prove bootability or application recovery.
Exact restore wizard choices depend on your Veeam version, destination and workload. Record these with the backup owner before the change; do not improvise an in-place production restore. Return to the rollback gate only when the documented recovery objective is achievable.
expected: The intended VM has a verified new restore point and a documented, tested recovery path. No infrastructure command is executed by the course itself.

title: Choose one device or an approved subnet
where: Work Windows computer · network plan
actions:
One IPv4 address uses /32, such as 192.0.2.50/32. A subnet is a range, such as 10.20.30.0/24. These are examples only. Get the real source range and approval from the network owner.
A vSphere port group is not itself an IP subnet. Confirm the VLAN, subnet and routing used by the VMs attached to it. Allowing a subnet allows any device with a matching source address, not just VMs with a particular port-group name.
If the manager also runs in vSphere, there is no Azure NSG on that VM. Review RHEL firewalld and the actual network/NSX firewalls. If the manager is in Azure, also review its NSGs.
With private routed connectivity to Azure, use the private source range only if that range is actually preserved. With a public internet connection, Azure normally sees the company firewall’s translated public address. Use the confirmed public address or addresses, not an unreachable private range. One shared public address can represent devices outside the intended port group too.
expected: You know the source address the manager really sees. You are changing dashboard HTTPS access only, not SSH access.
